messages:
lina: Hey team, running a POC with AcmeCorp. They're sending logs/traces from a Windows service via Fluentd -> our hosted API and hitting 429s when they batch. Also trace IDs aren't showing up in Console. Can someone help triage? cc @marta @ben :wave:

marta: Do we have the Fluentd config + an example payload they send? Also which SDK/agent on Windows?

lina: They attached a small snippet from their Fluentd http output plugin and a failing request sample. Using fluent-plugin-out-http on Win Server 2019. Example request body (trimmed):

```
{"events":[{"message":"user event...","trace_id":"abc-123"}, {"message":"another","trace_id":"abc-123"}]}
```

And response: 429 with body `{\"error\":\"rate_limit_exceeded\"}` and header `Retry-After: 10`.

ben: Ok quick checklist: 1) server is bundling multiple events -> large payloads can trigger our per-request token quota 2) We honor Retry-After and return 429 when throughput cap hit for that key/route 3) trace propagation: we look for standard headers (traceparent/x-request-id) or an explicit `trace_id` field in JSON but Fluentd plugin might not map it by default.

raj: For trace IDs we recommend adding a static header mapping in the Fluentd HTTP output so each request carries `X-Request-Id` or `traceparent`. Example header in fluent config: `headers { "X-Request-Id": "${record[\"trace_id\"]}" }` (depends on plugin syntax). When Console receives that header we index it as the routed trace id.

marta: Also two operational fixes to unblock the POC quickly: reduce batch_size to ~20 events per request OR set `chunk_limit_size` lower on Fluentd so each HTTP chunk is < 512 KB; and add exponential retry/backoff on 429. This will avoid triggering the token/throughput limiter.

lina: Here's the Fluentd snippet I sent them (they're using out_http):

```
<match app.logs>
  @type http
  endpoint https://api.redwood.ai/v1/logs
  serializer json
  <request_headers>
    Content-Type: application/json
    X-Request-Id: ${record["trace_id"]}
    Authorization: Bearer ${ENV['RW_API_KEY']}
  </request_headers>
  <buffer>
    @type memory
    chunk_limit_size 1m
    flush_interval 5s
  </buffer>
</match>
```

ben: Two more practical tips: 1) If they can't change agent quickly, add a small proxy (nginx) to inject X-Request-Id from body into header for the outgoing request. 2) Monitor `x-rw-rate-limit` / `Retry-After` headers in responses to tune client.

observability-bot: FYI: I created a quick trace-view bookmark: Console > Observability > Traces?query=x-request-id:abc-123 -> https://console.redwood.ai/traces?q=x-request-id:abc-123 (internal link).

olivia: If they want to correlate logs->requests in Console: use the same header value for both log events and request traces. When you search `x-request-id:abc-123` in Logs or Traces it will join. For long term we recommend adding `traceparent` and adopting W3C tracecontext.

marta: For the POC, give them a short config to stop batching and add retry: set `chunk_limit_size 256k`, `retry_limit 8`, and `retry_wait 2s` in Fluentd buffer. That usually clears 429s for small throughput.

lina: Thanks — passing this back to Acme. One question: is there any per-key daily quota we should warn them about?

ben: Yes there are soft throughput caps and a daily usage cap on trial keys. I'll DM billing to confirm their key tier. For immediate testing they can use a dedicated test key with higher limits if sales approves.

lina: Great, will ask for a temp key. I'll update the customer with the Fluentd snippet + reduce batch and backoff. Will report back after retry. :thumbsup:

marta: If they still see missing trace IDs after header injection, paste a raw request sample and we'll debug header mapping.

lina: Will do. Thanks everyone.
